correctness.rationale: Integration from F=0 gives Kt=B g(F/B), g(u)=u−log(1+u), a strictly increasing forward coordinate for F>0. With u=F₁/B the inverse reduces to Rρ(u)=g(ρu)/g(u)=q and then B=F₁/u, K=F₁g(u)/(t₁u). For h=ug′/g, an independent check is h(u)⁻¹=∫₀¹ s(1+u)/(1+us) ds, whose derivative is the integral of s(1−s)/(1+us)² and is strictly positive. Thus u(log Rρ)′=h(ρu)−h(u)<0. The limits are ρ² and ρ, so neither equality endpoint yields finite positive parameters. As u→0, g=u²/2−u³/3+O(u⁴) gives δ∼2ρ²(ρ−1)u/3, giving the claimed reciprocal-depth and linear-conductivity laws. As u→∞, the exact ratio difference is [ρ log(1+u)−log(1+ρu)]/g(u), so ε∼(ρ−1)log(u)/u and log(1/ε)/log(u)→1. This verifies the logarithmic correction in B and the linear K-deficit with their stated leading constants. Independent bounded checks of the rational derivative identity, the u=1 example and both asymptotic regimes agreed (slower convergence on the logarithmic side). The uploaded script was inspected, not executed. The asymptotics fix F₁,t₁ and ρ>1; the conclusion identifies the product capillary length only and does not assert inference from noisy data.
